en: front panel of a garment; front hem

examples.en: I spilled coffee on the front of my skirt.
I held the front of my hanbok and walked slowly.
The front of my coat is flapping in the strong wind.

examples.ko: 그는 윗옷 앞자락을 여미고 밖으로 나갔어요.
examples.en: He pulled the front of his jacket closed and went outside.

examples.ko: 아이가 울면서 엄마 치마 앞자락에 매달렸어요.
examples.en: The child cried and clung to the front of her mother's skirt.

examples.ko: 비를 맞아서 윗옷 앞자락이 다 젖었어요.
examples.en: I got rained on, and the front of my top is all wet.

explain: 치마, 저고리, 두루마기처럼 늘어지는 옷의 앞쪽 아랫부분을 말해요. 반대말은 '뒷자락'이에요.

phrases.en: The front hem of my clothes got soaked in the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한복뿐 아니라 길게 늘어지는 옷에 두루 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Usable not only for hanbok but for any long, hanging garment.

phrases.example: 바람에 날릴까 봐 앞자락을 꼭 잡았어요.
phrases.en: I held the front hem tightly so the wind wouldn't blow it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이 날리거나 끌리지 않게 잡는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes holding a garment so it won't blow or drag.

phrases.example: 물을 건너려고 치마 앞자락을 걷어 올렸어요.
phrases.en: I lifted my skirt's front hem to cross the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치마나 두루마기를 걷을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when lifting up a skirt or long coat.
phrases.en_equiv: to hitch up the front hem

explain_en: It refers to the lower front part of hanging garments such as skirts, jeogori and overcoats. The opposite is '뒷자락'.

en: to pull together and fasten (clothes, collar); to tidy one's attire

examples.en: The wind was cold, so I pulled my collar closed.
Grandma straightened and fastened my clothes for me.
I collected myself and decided to start again.

examples.ko: 면접 전에 단추를 채우고 옷깃을 여미는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Before an interview, it's good to button up and straighten your collar.
If you close your coat, you'll feel less cold.
She tucked her skirt neatly and sat down.

explain: 옷의 벌어진 부분을 모아 단정하게 하는 일이에요. 단추를 '잠그다'와 달리 앞을 모아 매무새를 바로잡는 느낌이 있어요. '옷깃을 여미다'가 가장 흔하고, '마음을 여미다'처럼 마음가짐을 바로잡을 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I straightened myself with solemn respect in front of the patriots who died for the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 옷을 정리하는 것 외에, 경건하고 엄숙한 마음가짐을 갖출 때 비유로 써요. 글이나 연설에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Besides actually adjusting clothes, it is used figuratively for taking a respectful, solemn attitude. It often appears in writing and speeches.

explain_en: It means gathering the loose parts of clothing to look neat. Unlike '잠그다' (to fasten buttons), it carries the sense of pulling the front together and tidying up. '옷깃을 여미다' is the most common, and it is also used for composing one's mind, as in '마음을 여미다'.

en: to purse; to pucker; to draw in

examples.en: Purse your lips and try whistling.
I cupped my hands and scooped up stream water to drink.
The baby curled its fingers and then opened them.
He was embarrassed and pursed his mouth.
The flower closes up its petals in the evening.
If you sit with your legs together, there's enough room.

explain: 반대말은 '벌리다'나 '펴다'예요. 입, 손, 꽃잎, 다리처럼 벌어진 것을 안쪽으로 모을 때 써요. 스스로 줄어드는 건 '오므라들다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Purse your lips and make an 'oo' sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발음을 연습하거나 휘파람을 불 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when practicing pronunciation or whistling.

phrases.en: Try closing and opening your fingers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '펴다'와 이어서 반복 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with its opposite 'to open out' to describe a repeated motion.

phrases.en: In a narrow seat, I sit with my legs together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벌어진 다리를 안쪽으로 모을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when bringing spread legs closer together.

explain_en: Its opposites are '벌리다' and '펴다'. It is used when you draw something open, like a mouth, hand, petals or legs, inward. For something that shrinks on its own, use '오므라들다'.

examples.en: It got hot, so we wear summer uniforms from today.

examples.ko: 하복은 보통 반팔 셔츠로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: Summer uniforms are usually short-sleeved shirts.

examples.ko: 동생이 하복을 사러 교복 가게에 갔어요.
examples.en: My younger brother went to the uniform shop to buy a summer uniform.
When June comes, our school switches to summer uniforms.
You have to attach a name tag to the summer uniform.

examples.ko: 작년에 산 하복이 작아져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The summer uniform I bought last year got too small, so I need a new one.

explain: 주로 교복이나 제복처럼 정해진 옷에 써요. 반대말은 '동복'이에요. 그냥 여름에 입는 옷은 '여름옷'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The summer school uniform is thin and cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하복'과 같은 뜻의 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say the same thing as 하복.

phrases.en: From June, everyone wears the summer uniform.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교복을 바꿔 입는 시기에 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for the time of year when uniforms change.

phrases.en: We change into summer uniforms starting next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동복에서 하복으로 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when switching from the winter uniform to the summer one.
phrases.en_equiv: to change into the summer uniform

explain_en: Lighter summer version of a school or work uniform. It is mainly used for set outfits such as school or work uniforms. Its opposite is '동복' (winter uniform). Ordinary clothes worn in summer are simply called '여름옷'.

examples.en: The mushy, bursting feeling was strange.
When I pressed it with my hand, it sank in squishily.
I don't like the mushy texture when I chew it.

examples.ko: 진흙 위를 걷자 발밑이 물컹물컹 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: When I walked on the mud, the ground felt squishy under my feet.
I overcooked it, so it turned mushy and fell apart.
I kneaded the soft, squishy dough with my hands.

explain: 손으로 누르거나 입에서 씹을 때 무르고 눌리는 느낌이 계속될 때 써요. '물컹물컹 씹히다', '물컹물컹 눌리다'처럼 동사 앞에 오고, '물컹물컹한'처럼 꾸며 줄 수도 있어요.

phrases.en: Mushy mushrooms don't taste good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 말로 써서 식감이 별로라는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to describe an unpleasant, mushy texture.

phrases.en: The eggplant feels mushy as I chew it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입 안에서 무르게 씹히는 식감을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a soft, squishy texture in the mouth.

phrases.en: The tomato felt squishy when I pressed it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손으로 누를 때 무르게 들어가는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something giving way softly under the hand.

explain_en: It is used when something feels soft and squishy over and over as you press it or chew it. It comes before verbs, as in '물컹물컹 씹히다' and '물컹물컹 눌리다', and can also modify a noun as '물컹물컹한'.

t90.ax: The mushy, bursting feeling was strange.

examples.ko: 엄마가 끓여 준 비지찌개가 정말 맛있었어요.
examples.en: The bean curd dregs stew my mom made was really delicious.

examples.ko: 두부를 만들 때 비지가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: A lot of bean curd dregs come out when making tofu.

examples.ko: 비지에 김치와 돼지고기를 넣고 끓여 먹어요.
examples.en: We boil it with kimchi and pork added to the bean curd dregs.

examples.ko: 시장에서 비지를 싸게 팔길래 한 봉지 샀어요.
examples.en: Bean curd dregs were being sold cheaply at the market, so I bought a bag.

examples.ko: 비지는 고소하고 부드러워서 겨울에 먹기 좋아요.
examples.en: Bean curd dregs are nutty and soft, so they're good to eat in winter.

examples.ko: 비지 요리는 처음 먹어 봤는데 괜찮았어요.
examples.en: I tried a bean curd dregs dish for the first time, and it was good.

explain: '비지찌개'로 가장 많이 먹고, '콩비지'라고도 해요. 소박한 집밥 느낌이 있는 음식이에요. 두부를 직접 만드는 가게에서 싸게 파는 경우도 있어요.

phrases.en: On cold days I crave warm bean curd dreg stew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비지로 만든 대표적인 음식 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical dish made with 비지.

phrases.en: I bought a bag of soybean dregs at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 콩으로 만든 것임을 분명히 말하는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A name that makes clear it is made from soybeans.

phrases.en: If you add bean curd dregs to the stew, the taste gets milder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 재료로 넣는다는 뜻으로 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used for adding it as a cooking ingredient.

explain_en: It is most often eaten as '비지찌개' (a stew) and is also called '콩비지'. It is a food with a simple home-cooked feel. Shops that make tofu themselves sometimes sell it cheaply.

examples.en: Slice the green onion into small rounds and put it in the soup.
I sliced the cucumber into thin rounds and put it in the gimbap.
I cut the chili pepper into small rounds and added it to the ramyeon.
I slice zucchini into thin rounds and make soybean paste stew.

examples.ko: 대파를 송송 썰어 두면 요리할 때 편해요.
examples.en: If you slice scallions ahead of time, it's convenient when cooking.

examples.ko: 송송 썬 김치를 넣고 볶음밥을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made fried rice with finely chopped kimchi.

explain: 주로 '송송 썰다'로 파, 고추, 오이처럼 가늘고 둥근 재료를 잘게 써는 모양을 말해요. 큼직하게 썰 때는 '숭덩숭덩'을 써요. 요리법에서 정말 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Please slice the green onion into thin rounds.
phrases.nuance_ko: '송송'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb most often paired with 'songsong'.

phrases.en: I put chopped green onion in the ramen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 썰어 놓은 재료를 말할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form for ingredients that have been sliced.

phrases.example: 송송 썬 고추를 국에 넣으면 칼칼해요.
phrases.en: Adding sliced chili to the soup makes it spicy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고추도 둥글게 얇게 썰 때 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for chili sliced into thin rounds.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '송송 썰다', describing slicing thin, round ingredients like scallions, chili peppers and cucumbers into small pieces. For big chunky cuts, people say '숭덩숭덩'. It appears very often in recipes.

en: millet and red bean rice cake

examples.en: We always prepare susupat-tteok for a child's first birthday party.
My grandmother made susupat-tteok for me.
Susupat-tteok is red on the outside and chewy.

examples.ko: 생일마다 수수팥떡을 해 주시던 어머니가 생각나요.
examples.en: I remember my mother who made susupat-tteok every birthday.
I shared susupat-tteok with the neighbors.
The susupat-tteok is still warm, so it's delicious.

explain: 아이의 돌잔치나 생일에 해 주는 떡으로 알려져 있어요. 붉은 팥과 수수의 붉은색이 나쁜 기운을 막아 준다는 믿음에서 만든다고 해요. 한국 음식이나 풍습 이야기에서 만날 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Mom made sorghum and red bean rice cakes for the child's birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떡을 직접 만든다고 할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing for making the rice cake yourself.
phrases.en_equiv: to make sorghum red bean cake

phrases.en: I tried sorghum red bean cake at a first-birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 경험을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for talking about eating it.
phrases.en_equiv: to eat sorghum red bean cake

phrases.en: We shared sorghum red bean cake with the neighbors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌이나 생일에 떡을 이웃과 함께 나누는 풍습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the custom of sharing the cake with neighbors on a birthday.
phrases.en_equiv: to share sorghum red bean cake

explain_en: It is known as a rice cake made for a child's first birthday party or birthdays. It is said to be made from the belief that the red color of red beans and sorghum keeps bad energy away. You may meet it when talking about Korean food and customs.

examples.ko: 이 치즈는 풍미가 깊어서 빵과 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: This cheese has a rich flavor and goes well with bread.

examples.ko: 갓 볶은 커피는 풍미가 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: Freshly roasted coffee has a really good aroma and taste.

examples.ko: 버터를 넣으면 풍미를 훨씬 살릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Adding butter brings out the flavor much more.
Soy sauce aged for a long time has a different depth of flavor.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 풍미 가득한 수프로 유명해요.
examples.en: This shop is famous for its soup full of flavor.

examples.ko: 풍미를 놓치지 않으려면 약한 불에서 천천히 구워요.
examples.en: To keep the flavor, grill it slowly over low heat.

explain: '맛'에 향까지 어우러진 느낌이어서 음식이나 커피, 치즈 같은 것을 소개할 때 자주 써요. '풍미가 깊다/좋다/가득하다'처럼 말하고, 일상 대화에서는 '맛있다'가 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요. '한 시대를 풍미하다'의 풍미하다와는 쓰임이 달라요.

phrases.en: Butter adds flavor to the bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료나 양념이 맛과 향을 더 좋게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an ingredient or seasoning improves taste and aroma.

phrases.en: My mouth is full of coffee flavor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛과 향이 아주 풍부하게 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when taste and aroma feel rich and abundant.

phrases.example: 풍미 좋은 차를 한 잔 마셨어요.
phrases.en: I drank a cup of tea with a lovely flavor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 음료 앞에 붙여서 칭찬하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a food or drink noun as praise.

explain_en: Overall flavor and aroma, esp. coffee, wine, food (풍미가 깊다) It means taste combined with aroma, and is often used when introducing food, coffee or cheese, as in '풍미가 깊다/좋다/가득하다'. In casual talk, '맛있다' often sounds more natural. It is different from the verb in '한 시대를 풍미하다'.

t90.ax: Adding butter brings out the flavor much more.

examples.en: That painter lived in the countryside in his later years.
I'm saving money from now so my later years will be comfortable.
My grandfather's final years were not lonely.

examples.ko: 작가의 말년 작품은 아주 조용하고 깊어요.
examples.en: The author's late works are very quiet and deep.
I want to spend my last years happily.
He never stopped writing until the end of his life.

explain: '노년'은 나이 든 시기를 가리키고, '말년'은 삶이나 일의 마지막 시기를 가리켜요. 보통 '말년에'로 쓰고, 어르신 앞에서 '말년'이라고 하면 실례가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 말년 병장이라서 요즘 일을 거의 안 해요.
phrases.en: a soldier near discharge who takes it easy
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 제대할 병장을 가리키는 군대 말이에요. 느긋하게 지내는 사람을 놀릴 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Military slang for a sergeant close to discharge; also used to tease someone who takes things easy.

explain_en: Final stretch of a person's life or a period (말년에) '노년' refers to old age, while '말년' points to the last stretch of a life or career. It is usually used as '말년에', and saying '말년' in front of an elderly person can be rude.

examples.en: This period was the heyday of Korean cinema's revival.
They say the 1990s were a golden revival period for Korean pop.
The city entered a period of revival, and people flocked to it.

examples.ko: 불교 문화의 부흥기에 많은 절이 지어졌어요.
examples.en: Many temples were built during the revival of Buddhist culture.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 요즘 새로운 부흥기를 누리고 있어요.
examples.en: That shop is enjoying a new boom these days.
Will a revival period come to our neighborhood again?

explain: '전성기'는 가장 잘나가던 때이고, '부흥기'는 약해졌다가 다시 힘차게 일어나는 시기에 더 잘 어울려요. 문화, 산업, 종교, 도시 이야기에 많이 쓰고 '맞이하다, 누리다'와 자주 함께 나와요.

phrases.en: That industry entered a new period of revival.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부흥의 시기가 시작될 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for when a revival period begins.
phrases.en_equiv: to enter a period of revival

phrases.example: 한국 영화는 지금 부흥기를 누리고 있어요.
phrases.en: Korean film is enjoying a revival now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 시기를 즐기고 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone is enjoying the good period.
phrases.en_equiv: to enjoy a period of revival

phrases.en: This era is called a period of cultural revival.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문화, 산업 같은 분야 이름과 함께 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works well with fields such as culture or industry.

explain_en: '전성기' is the peak time, while '부흥기' fits a time when something weak rises strongly again. It is common for culture, industry, religion and cities, and often goes with '맞이하다' and '누리다'.

en: the twelfth lunar month; December of the lunar calendar

examples.ko: 섣달이 되면 한 해가 다 갔다는 생각이 들어요.
examples.en: When Seotdal comes, I feel the year is nearly over.

examples.ko: 섣달 그믐날에는 가족이 모여 밤을 새웠어요.
examples.en: On the last night of Seotdal, the family gathered and stayed up all night.
The cold of Seotdal is truly biting.
It snowed a lot this Seotdal.
In Seotdal the market is crowded with Lunar New Year shoppers.
Once Seotdal passes, the new year comes soon.

explain: 음력 12월을 가리키는 옛 느낌의 말이에요. 보통 음력 마지막 날인 '섣달그믐'으로 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '12월'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I did not go to bed early on the last night of the year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음력 마지막 날을 가리키는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common use, meaning the last day of the lunar year.
phrases.en_equiv: last day of the lunar year

phrases.en: In the twelfth lunar month, we start preparing for the New Year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '음력'을 붙이면 달력의 달이라는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 음력 makes it clear that it is the lunar calendar month.

phrases.en: It snowed a lot in the twelfth month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한겨울의 날씨를 옛 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to talk about midwinter weather with an old-fashioned feel.

explain_en: It is an old-fashioned word for the twelfth lunar month. It mostly appears in '섣달그믐' (the last day of the lunar year), and in daily talk people simply say '12월'.

examples.ko: 세밑이 가까워 오니 고향에 가고 싶은 마음이 간절해져요.
examples.en: As the end of the year draws near, I long more and more to go home.
The expressways are very congested at the end of the year.

examples.ko: 올해 세밑은 가족과 조용히 보낼 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to spend this year's end quietly with my family.

examples.ko: 세밑 분위기 때문인지 거리가 들떠 보여요.
examples.en: Maybe because of the year-end mood, the streets look excited.

examples.ko: 세밑에 이웃을 돕는 모금 활동이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many fundraising drives to help neighbors at the end of the year.
I called to give you my year-end greetings in advance.

explain: 한 해가 끝나 가는 12월 말쯤을 가리키고, '연말'보다 글이나 뉴스에서 좀 더 운치 있게 들려요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '연말'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: We will get together with family at the end of the year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '세밑' 대신 쓰는 평범한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ordinary word people use in place of 세밑 in conversation.

phrases.en: A year-end cold wave has arrived.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often heard in the news.

phrases.en: People send many gifts around the New Year season.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 해의 끝과 새해 시작을 함께 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the end of one year and the start of the next together.
phrases.en_equiv: the year-end and New Year season

explain_en: It points to the last days of December as the year ends, and it sounds a bit more literary than '연말' in writing and news. In everyday conversation people usually just say '연말'.

en: greeting the new year; seeing off the old year

examples.en: A year-end bell-ringing ceremony is held at Bosingak.

examples.ko: 송구영신 예배에 온 가족이 함께 갔어요.
examples.en: The whole family went to the New Year's Eve service together.

examples.ko: 송구영신이라는 말처럼 묵은해를 보내고 새해를 맞아요.
examples.en: As the phrase says, we send off the old year and welcome the new one.

examples.ko: 올해 송구영신은 집에서 조용히 보내고 싶어요.
examples.en: This year I want to spend New Year's Eve quietly at home.

examples.ko: 송구영신을 기념해 친구들과 해돋이를 보러 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: To mark the turn of the year, we decided to go watch the sunrise with friends.

examples.ko: 송구영신 인사를 보냈더니 친구가 바로 답장했어요.
examples.en: I sent a new year's greeting and my friend replied right away.

explain: 12월 31일 밤부터 새해로 넘어가는 때를 말하는 한자 성어예요. 타종 행사, 예배, 카드 문구처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '연말연시'나 '새해맞이'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Our family goes to the New Year's Eve service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 12월 31일 밤에 드리는 예배를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the service held on the night of December 31.

phrases.en: A year-end and new-year event is held in front of city hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새해를 맞는 공식 행사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for official events welcoming the new year.

phrases.en: I went to the sea with friends to welcome the new year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is more natural in everyday conversation.

explain_en: Formal four-character phrase; New Year's Eve, bidding old year farewell. It is a Chinese-character phrase for the time when the year turns over from the night of December 31. It often appears in formal settings such as bell-ringing events, services and card messages. In everyday talk, people more often say '연말연시' or '새해맞이'.
